correctness.rationale: Complete proof reconstructs all assumptions and quantifiers: goodness on bi-infinite periodic extension, minimal-antisquare classification with Proposition 18, eight-factor equivalence, run grammar (including 0, 2 or >=4 separating singleton runs for opposite long symbols), converse, marked-run double counting accounting for imprimitive periods, formal logarithmic zeta and weighted Möbius inversion, and exact equality densities. A standalone brute-force verifier checks 32,766 indexed words through n=14 by bounded-order direct antisquares, eight forbidden factors and the cyclic grammar, all polynomial coefficients, direct primitive orbit counts through n=12, and recurrence/support through n=80. The finite checks alone are not the infinite proof. Published Theorem 11 and Proposition 18 are indispensable cited premises.

originality.rationale: Direct comparisons were made against the source that already derives the minimal forbidden antisquare family and unweighted growth characteristic polynomial; those are acknowledged as prior, while the new exact two-variable periodic zeta, primitive weight spectra and sharp excluded density interval are not stated there. Accessible alternate papers concern a different circular constraint or linear avoidance. Semantic research-record queries for equivalent formulations and stronger coverage did not surface one. This is a best-evidence originality assessment, not a proof that no prior equivalent exists.
residual_risks: The 2022 Pansiot-code grammar may be convertible into a standard weighted transfer matrix; an unpublished or unindexed computation could already contain this exact rational specialization.

Published univariate recurrences and the exponential growth constant are prior results; only the exact cyclic weight refinement, necklace profiles and density-support interpretation are treated as potentially new.

value.rationale: Exact weight-resolved periodic-point counting is a natural dynamical invariant of the established good-word shift, stronger than its known linear growth exponent. The rational two-variable expression computes all weighted finite-period profiles and each primitive rotation-necklace weight enumerator. The two disjoint grammar components force a nontrivial density exclusion (1/3,2/3) with sharp six-rotation equality families, explaining the periodic constraint rather than a merely numerical census.
